sites.residue_label: C-terminal, immediately before GPI attachment site
sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG staining of transfected HEK-293T cells (L3); expression confirmed by Western blot (n=3, L4); no functional assay reported.
sites.rationale: LYPD2 is a GPI-anchored protein with no TM domain; the signal peptide (residues 1–22) is cleaved and the C-terminus is GPI-anchored, leaving exactly one viable surface tag position: immediately before the GPI signal. L2 explicitly places the FLAG tag at this junction ('immediately N-terminal to the predicted GPI attachment residue'), and L3 confirms the tagged protein reaches the cell surface. Because the GPI omega-site residue number is not stated in the paper, insert_after_residue is null and the position is topology_derived from the single available C-terminal extracellular junction. Full-length M. musculus and R. norvegicus lypd2 constructs carrying a FLAG epitope placed immediately N-terminal to the predicted GPI attachment residue (as determined by mendel.imp.ac.at/gpi) were expressed in HEK-293T cells. Surface display was confirmed by anti-FLAG staining (L3); expression confirmed by Western blot (L4). The exact omega-site residue number is not stated in the paper.

sources.claim: HEK-293T cells were transfected with the indicated amounts of each construct and stained for presence of C-terminal FLAG epitope.

LY6D and LYPD2 were tagged C-terminally with an HA tag.
293T cells were cultivated in Dulbecco's modified Eagle Medium (DMEM; Invitrogen) supplemented with 10% heat-inactivated fetal bovine serum (FBS) and 50 μg/ml gentamycin. 293T cells (3 × 10 6 cells) were cotransfected with 20 μg total of DNA (empty pCI vector + increasing amounts of pCI vector containing the gene of interest) using the calcium phosphate technique.

literature_notes: LYPD2 (125 aa) has a signal peptide (1–22) and is GPI-anchored with no TM domain; the entire mature sequence (23–125) is extracellular. The only viable surface tag position is the C-terminal junction immediately before the GPI signal, which is the position both ledger papers used. No ledger line supports an N-terminal tag (the N-terminus is cleaved with the signal peptide and no paper describes a tag there), nor any internal loop insertion. L4 (Western blot confirmation of FLAG constructs) is from the same paper as L2/L3 and provides additional expression evidence for Site 1 but does not constitute a separate site. The exact GPI omega-site residue for LYPD2 is not stated in any ledger line; running the GPI prediction server (mendel.imp.ac.at) on the canonical sequence would be required to pin insert_after_residue precisely.
